surface_mechanism_description: The reaction mechanism involves the proton transfer from surface hydroxyl groups to the ligand, releasing neutral iPrCpH and leading to the formation of CeO2. The decomposition of the iPr-amd ligand during the precursor dose at reactor temperature contributes to the background signal.
evidence: Figure 5(a) shows the background subtracted mass spectrum during the Ce(iPrCp)2(iPr-amd) half cycle under optimum conditions. Consistent with the previous report for ALD using Gd(iprcp)3, all peaks can be linked to the fragmentation of the iPrCpH ligand, which indicates a proton transfer from the substrate surface hydroxyl groups to the ligand and the release of neutral iPrCpH. The peak at m/z = 108 corresponds to the iPrCpH, and peaks at m/z = 93, 91, 77, and 65 represent the loss of CHx from isopropyl chain. No signal from the iPr-amd ligand was detected during the ALD process, which can be attributed to the decomposition of the iPr-amd ligand during the precursor dose at the reactor temperature, leading to the inclusion of the decomposition products in the background signal.
